problems.title: Categories
problems.solution: Named things are lvalues; results of arithmetic are prvalues; std::move casts to an xvalue.

problems.title: std::move

options: casts v to an rvalue reference; nothing moves until a move constructor/assignment uses it

problems.solution: It's a cast. Without a receiving move operation, nothing happens.

problems.title: Named rvalue refs
problems.statement: void g(std::string&& s) { h(s); }, where h has overloads for const string& and string&&.

options: h(const string&): s is an lvalue inside g

problems.title: noexcept growth
problems.statement: std::vector<T> reallocates; T has a copy constructor and a move constructor that is not noexcept.

options: copied (move_if_noexcept chooses copy to keep the strong guarantee)

problems.solution: If a move threw halfway, the old buffer would be half-destroyed. Copying keeps the old buffer intact until success.

problems.title: Return statements

options: It prevents NRVO, forcing a move where there might have been no operation at all

hints: return local; already moves implicitly when elision doesn't happen.

problems.title: Const moves

options: a copy: const T&& binds to the copy constructor

hints: You can't steal from a const object.

problems.title: Sink parameters
problems.statement: Person(std::string name) : name_(std::move(name)) {} called with an lvalue string and with a temporary.

parts.prompt: Deep copies with an lvalue argument?

problems.solution: An lvalue is copied into the parameter, then moved; a temporary is moved (or elided) straight in.

problems.title: emplace surprise
hints: emplace forwards to the (explicit) size constructor.
problems.solution: emplace_back(10) calls vector(10), ten zeros. push_back({10}) uses the initializer list: one element.
